name: a(n) is the number of steps needed to reach a stable configuration in the 1D cellular automaton initialized with one cell with mass n and based on the rule "each cell gives half of its mass, rounded down, to its right neighbor".
comment: The cellular automaton is initialized with 1 cell with mass n. The evolution rule consists of each cell keeping half of its mass, rounded up (ceiling(mass / 2)), and giving half of its mass, rounded down (floor(mass / 2)), to its right neighbor. a(n) is the number of steps needed to reach the stable configuration made of n cells with mass 1.

Observations/conjectures: it appears that the finite difference of this sequence only contains 1's and 2's, that the runs of 2's are delimited by isolated 1's and tend to become larger and larger. One can probably write a(n) = 2*n - Sum_{k=1..n} I(k) where I(n) is the indicator function of some other sequence. See A305992.
Adamczewski includes a proof abstract regarding the above conjecture in linked article. - _Michael De Vlieger_, Aug 19 2026
link: Tom Adamczewski, OEIS Open: How many conjectures can language models turn into theorems?, arXiv:2608.11941 [cs.AI], 2026. See p. 14 (proof, Appendix A).
program: int main() { int n; for (n = 1; n <= N; n ++) { printf("%d, ", a(n)); } printf("\n"); }

(PARI) do(v) = {keep = vector(#v, k, ceil(v[k]/2)); move = vector(#v, k, floor(v[k]/2)); nv = vector(#v+1, k, if (k<=#v, keep[k], 0) + if (k==1, 0, move[k-1])); if (nv[#nv]==0, nv = vector(#nv-1, k, nv[k])); nv;}
a(n) = {vs = [n]; vend = vector(n, k, 1); nb = 0; while(vs != vend, vs = do(vs); nb++); nb;} \\ _Michel Marcus_, Jul 02 2018

(PARI) a(n) = {my(v=[n], res=0); while(Set(v)!=[1], res++; v = concat([ceil(v[1] / 2), vector(#v-1, i, v[i]\2 + ceil(v[i+1]/2)), vector(v[#v] > 1, k, v[#v] \ 2)])); res} \\ _David A. Corneth_, Jul 03 2018
